fix: src/render/stage.js, the streak mesh at ~line 1483-1517 and streakLen at 1593. Stop drawing the streak as a `PlaneGeometry(1,1)` scaled to `2.2*halfV*camera.aspect` -- that is a frustum-spanning billboard at one depth, which is why one uniform CoC and one uniform width is the physically CORRECT answer to the wrong geometry. Build it instead from the blade's actual swipe segment in world space: give the quad a near end and a far end at different z (the swipe crosses the frustum, so its ends are genuinely at different distances down the lens), and set its half-width per-vertex from the perspective divide rather than from a constant. You already have both halves of the machinery -- `cocPixelsNode(dist)` for the depth-varying blur and `lineDefocus(r0, dist)` for the flux-conserving 1-D widen. Acceptance, on the SHIPPED hero through `probes.py lens 00-hero.png`, discarding the sample whose position lands inside the subject mask: ribbon FWHM max/min > 4 (today 1.37 over the eight clean samples, plate-01 is 9.33) while edge_1090_p50 comes back DOWN toward 2 (today 4.513, plate-01 1.72) -- the plate's streak is width-varying and sharp, not uniform and soft, and r6 overshot past it. Then wire the second ribbon: delete blade.js's clipZ/clipW focal-plane pin (blade.js:118-131) and drive the trail band's vertices through `api.lens.line(halfWidthPx, -viewZ)` at each trail sample's real depth, so `probes.py lens 09-combo+50ms.png` stops returning edge 1.183 and edge 7.519 from ribbon samples 71 px apart in the same frame. Leave the lights, the exposure and the black floor alone -- `void` shows the floor sits inside plate-01's own corner range and 01-whole-watermelon's key/rim/falloff is the strongest thing in the round.
